sources.entry: BrowBro - Keyboard-first macOS menu bar app to open clicked links in the right browser or profile.

summary.one_liner: BrowBro is a macOS app that lets you pick which browser or Chrome profile opens a link you click on the web.
summary.what_it_does: BrowBro is a macOS application that lets the user choose the browser they want to use to open a web link. The listing describes it as a keyboard-first menu bar app that opens clicked links in the right browser or profile. The README mentions that BrowBro reads Chrome profiles, which is how it finds them, and that it asks for macOS permission to read other apps' data for this. The README is short and does not detail the interface or the full feature set. It also describes an auto-update mechanism via Sparkle and a separate Mac App Store build.
use_cases: choose which browser opens a link
open a link in a specific Chrome profile
keyboard-driven link opening from the menu bar
switch between multiple browsers on a Mac
install a macOS menu bar utility via Homebrew
how_to_run: Or download the DMG from the latest GitHub release and drag BrowBro into Applications
Or install BrowBro from the Mac App Store (sandboxed build)
notable: Keyboard-first menu bar app for macOS
Opens links in a chosen browser or Chrome profile
Signed with Apple Developer ID and notarized
Self-updates via Sparkle, with a separate sandboxed Mac App Store build
Marketing site in site/ published to GitHub Pages
caveats: Needs macOS permission to read other apps' data to find Chrome profiles
Mac App Store build is sandboxed: Chrome profiles need a one-time folder grant, and settings start over when switching builds
